observation_summary: The application throws an OutOfMemoryError when processing a large number of weights because it creates a full n x n matrix for what is essentially a diagonal weight vector.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the underlying data structure used to represent the weight matrix from a full matrix (which consumes O(n^2) memory) to a DiagonalMatrix (which consumes O(n) memory). This is a change in the computational strategy/algorithm used to store and process the weights, rather than a simple initialization fix or a missing guard. The logic for creating the weight matrix was inefficient for the given input size, requiring a procedural change to how the matrix is constructed and subsequently processed (in the squareRoot method).
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'When using the Weigth class to pass a large number of weights to multivariate vector optimizers, an nxn full matrix is created (and copied) when a n elements vector is used. This exhausts memory when n is large.'
The fix diff shows replacing the creation of a full matrix with a DiagonalMatrix in the Weight constructor.
The fix diff shows adding a specialized path for DiagonalMatrix in the squareRoot method of AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes how the weightMatrix is initialized, the root cause is the choice of a full matrix data structure for a diagonal problem, which is an algorithmic/design choice for the data representation.
This is not a missing capability; the system could already handle weights, just inefficiently. It is a local optimization of the data structure used for the computation.
